subject: Follow-up: compact pilot outline and success criteria for Peregrine Commerce
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@peregrinecommerce.com>, Nina Patel <nina.patel@peregrinecommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: compact pilot outline and success criteria for Peregrine Commerce

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion and clear goals. Per our call, I put together a compact 4-week pilot (POC) proposal focused on validating latency-sensitive catalog search and relevance improvement with Redwood inference. High-level plan below; full checklist attached (redwood-compact-poc-checklist.pdf).

Goal: demonstrate 30% reduction in average query latency at 95th percentile and 10-15% lift in checkout-add rate from relevance improvements on targeted SKUs.

Proposed scope (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (pre-kick): networking + creds + sample data ingest (engineering prep)
- Week 1: baseline collection + model variant A (off-the-shelf quantized) evaluation on 1M sessions
- Week 2: model variant B (light-tuned) + routing/caching configs, compare A/B
- Week 3: integration smoke tests + live shadow run on 5% traffic for 48 hours
- Week 4: analysis, handoff, and recommendations (report + next-step options)

Success criteria (pass/fail gates):
- Latency: 95p token latency <= 120ms in staged environment under production-like QPS
- Relevance: minimum +10% lift in add-to-cart rate on target SKUs vs baseline
- Stability: no more than 1% error rate and graceful fallback to existing service
- Operability: Redwood console traces + token-level cost estimates available to your SREs

Owners & asks:
- Peregrine: provide a sandbox dataset extract (sample sessions, product catalog) and a small network allowlist for our infra team – point of contact: Oliver or Nina
- Redwood (Ben): model onboarding and infra prep
- Redwood (Marissa): success metrics dashboard + weekly check-ins

Next steps (try to keep cadence tight):
1) Confirm scope + sign the compact SOW (attached SOW-peregrine-docusign.docx) — target to have signed by 2027-07-02
2) Kickoff call (30 min) to align on data handoff: propose 2027-07-05 10:00 PT
3) Pre-kick checklist completed by 2027-07-08

If that looks good I’ll send the DocuSign link and schedule the kickoff. Open to trimming scope if you prefer a narrower 3-week run; just flag which checkpoints to compress.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Follow-up: compact pilot outline and success criteria for Peregrine Commerce

Thanks Chloe — appreciate the clear write-up. Quick notes from our side after syncing with SRE:
- The timeline looks achievable but we need the network allowlist details earlier (SRE wants IP ranges + ports by 2027-07-01). Can you confirm your infra contact?
- On success criteria: the add-to-cart uplift target is fine but can we measure both conversion lift and query abandonment rate? Both matter for product ops.
- For the shadow run, can we cap traffic at 3% initially for risk reasons, then move to 5% if stable?

We’ll aim to sign the compact SOW quickly — Nina will own internal approvals. Also looping in our security reviewer if you can share a short statement of data handling and retention for the pilot (SOC2 scope, retention window).

Oliver
Director of Product Operations, Peregrine Commerce
oliver.grant@peregrinecommerce.com | +1 (212) 555-0147

- Metrics: agree to include conversion lift and query-abandonment delta as secondary success metrics; marissa will add both to the dashboard and track daily
- Shadow run cadence: agree to 3% initial cap, escalate to 5% after 48 hours if error rates stay under 0.5%

Next actions I’m taking:
- I’ll initiate DocuSign flow for the compact SOW this morning (expect Docusign link in the next hour)

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.
